report.question: Do released artifacts, error messages, stack traces and logs disclose the owner's username, home path, machine name, private repository names or internal hostnames?
report.answer: YES for three of the five identity classes, and the two mechanisms need DIFFERENT fixes. (1) The BUILT bundle discloses only the USERNAME, and the two-profile differential proves every one of those 22 hits is HARDCODED (byte-identical archive across profiles) - author field, LICENSE holder, and 19 schema $id URIs on the owner-derived domain prekzursil.dev. (2) The RUNTIME surface is where the HOME PATH leaks, invisibly to any static scan: 5 of 21 error-message cases and 4 of 9 identity-token-free cases printed C:\Users\Prekzursil\..., and an unhandled exception prints a full traceback naming the absolute install path three times while exiting with a bare 1. (3) The log redactor strips credentials but has no identity rule, so a logged path ships verbatim. (4) MACHINE NAME was not emitted on any measured surface. (5) PRIVATE REPO NAMES and INTERNAL HOSTNAMES appear only in the release/ staging workspace (74 identity occurrences, 127.0.0.1:8089, localhost:4000), which the current payload projection does NOT ship.

verdict_per_enumerated_target.where: shipped bundle: 22 of 45 members (plugin.json author, LICENSE, build.py embedded LICENSE, 19 schema $id + schemas.BASE_URI on https://prekzursil.dev/); release/ workspace: 74 occurrences; runtime error messages and traceback; survives log redaction
verdict_per_enumerated_target.mechanism: HARDCODED in the bundle (proven by the byte-identical two-profile rebuild); INTERPOLATED at render time in errors, tracebacks and logs
verdict_per_enumerated_target.severity: P3 in the bundle (author/licence attribution is arguably intended publication metadata, but it is byte-identical to the OS account name, which is what makes every path leak cross-linkable); P2 via the traceback path

PRESENT in 4 release/ files, in 5 of 21 runtime error messages, in 4 of 9 identity-token-free amplification cases, in the unhandled-exception traceback (3 frame lines), and unredacted through the log sink
verdict_per_enumerated_target.mechanism: INTERPOLATED at runtime only - invisible to the static scan, which is precisely the case the unit's evidence_requirement predicted

verdict_per_enumerated_target.where: zero hits across 45 bundle members, 14 release files, 30 runtime invocations and 1 traceback
verdict_per_enumerated_target.mechanism: n/a - not emitted. Scoped inline: an exhaustive Logger call-site census was NOT run, and the redactor probe proves the hostname would NOT be stripped if some path did log it (UNVERIFIED for that residual, settling experiment recorded).

verdict_per_enumerated_target.mechanism: HARDCODED loopback endpoints. No routable or corporate-internal hostname was found. The literal token list MISSED these two - the independent shape matcher found them, and that under-specification is disclosed rather than hidden.

fix_classes.hardcoded_tokens_bundle: Edit the source constants, not the environment: platform/plugin/build.py manifest_for() author={'name': 'Prekzursil'} and the embedded _LICENSE copyright line, plus platform/plugin/schemas.py BASE_URI='https://prekzursil.dev/ast-integrate/schema'. Note a $id change is a schema-identity change and must be versioned, not silently rewritten.
fix_classes.runtime_interpolation: Different fix, same finding family: relativise or elide absolute paths in PluginError.render (print the path relative to the supplied root, or a <prefix>/... placeholder), and add a top-level `except Exception` in cli.main() that renders a classified E_* block instead of letting the interpreter print frame paths.
fix_classes.log_sink: Add an identity rule to platform/plugin/logs.py redact_text: rewrite any absolute user-home path to <home> and any value equal to the OS account name / hostname to a placeholder, before the credential rules run.
fix_classes.release_workspace: release/platforms/windows/* are machine-specific configs, not portable launchers. Either template the home path (${USERPROFILE}) or move them out of the release workspace before any packaging step is allowed to project release/**.

extensions.COVERAGE: MEASURED: identity token set (5 classes, 28 literal tokens, 5 encodings); the built release bundle (45 members, both profiles); the release/ staging workspace (14 tracked files); 30 runtime CLI invocations across the error taxonomy; 1 unhandled-exception traceback; the log redactor, executed. NOT MEASURED and disclosed in residual_unknowns: 12 of 17 error-taxonomy codes never triggered; no exhaustive Logger call-site census; no compiled/minified/source-map members exist in the real bundle so that capability is proven only against the synthetic control; org-owned private repos are outside the probed name set.
extensions.SELF_HASH_CAVEAT: artifacts[0].sha256 is the CANONICAL SELF-EXCLUDING hash (this file with the 64 hex characters of that field replaced by 64 zeros), because a self-referential file has no hash fixed point. `bytes` is exact and re-measurable. A reducer that naively re-hashes will report condition 3 as a sha256 mismatch; that is expected and is disclosed here rather than left to look like drift.
extensions.PROBE_INDEPENDENCE: PROBE 1 reads the BYTES of a built artifact with a Python literal-token matcher; its verifier is a grep shape-regex over the extracted tree (different tool, different matching principle). PROBE 2 runs 30 fresh interpreter PROCESSES and reads what they print; its verifier is a second process battery whose argv is guaranteed identity-token-free, plus a direct read of cli.main()'s handler set. No verdict rests on re-running its own source probe.
extensions.SCRIPTS: All probe scripts are under %TEMP%/adv0041/ (scan_identity.py, mkprofileB.py, mkcontrol.py, runtime_errors.py, runtime_amplify.py, runtime_traceback.py, logs_redaction_probe.py, build_artifact.py). They are scratch by the unit's hard constraints; every command line needed to re-derive the result is recorded verbatim in the probes above. RUN-2 scripts under %TEMP%/adv0041v/: reverify.py (holed, kept as the bad state), reverify2.py (decode-then-scan), runtime2.py (pass 2, crash probe faulty), runtime3.py (pass 3, liveness-marked crash probe + handled-exception control), codex_refuter_prompt.txt, patch1.py. Outputs: c2_ship.json, c2_bad.json, c2_good.json, rt2.json, rt3.json.
extensions.RUN2_INDEPENDENCE: Run 2 is same-vendor (anthropic) and therefore does NOT satisfy the catalogued reviewer_requirement, which demands a cross-vendor openai/Codex refuter. It is recorded as corroboration, not as review. Run 2's value is that it used a DIFFERENT matcher implementation (decode-then-scan vs run-1's scanner), a DIFFERENT environment (neutralised profile with the home dir outside the owner home, removing an echo confound run-1 did not control for), and a DIFFERENT crash-probe construction - and it found two faults in its own instruments before reporting.

failure.reason: All probes, controls and verdicts are MEASURED and recorded. What is missing is the catalogued cross-vendor (openai/Codex) refuter and the downstream-consumer execution; until those land the unit is not offered as complete.
